title: ContextAnalysisResult
description: Semantic interpretation of a Context Packet, written by the host agent (Context Analysis Agent). Base every statement on the packet. Keep observations and inferences separate: a claim is `observed` only when a packet evidence item or packet file directly states it; anything you reasoned out is `inferred`. Agentic inferences must never be presented as observed facts. Questions you cannot answer from the packet go in `unknowns`; disagreeing sources go in `conflicts`; missing project files you need go in `additionalContextRequests`. Do not list general engineering knowledge you already have as unknowns.

runId.description: Copy exactly from the Context Packet's `runId`.

technology.description: Technology relevant to the task, normalised to plain names (with versions where known), e.g. `TypeScript 5.4`.

architecture.description: How the repository is organised, as it bears on the task.

patterns.description: Architectural patterns, e.g. `hexagonal: adapters under src/adapters`.

conventions.description: Coding, naming, error-handling and testing conventions the task must follow.

dependencies.description: Dependencies that matter for the task (internal modules or external packages).

taskContext.description: What the task touches in this repository.

relevantComponents.description: Components, directories or files the task will touch (prefer repository-relative paths).

existingImplementations.description: Existing code that already does something similar and should be followed or reused.

constraints.description: Project-specific constraints the work must respect.

expectedOutcome.description: What done looks like for this task, if it can be determined.

evidence.description: Claims supporting the analysis. Each must cite a source present in the Context Packet.

claim.description: One factual statement, e.g. `Webhook handlers verify signatures with stripe.webhooks.constructEvent`.

source.description: Either a packet evidence id (`ev_…`) or a repository-relative path that appears in the packet (instructions, configuration, sourceFiles, evidence sources, existingSkills, structure, framework sources). A `:line` or `#Lline` suffix is allowed. An `observed` claim whose source is not in the packet is rejected.

type.description: `observed`: directly stated by the cited source. `inferred`: your reasoned conclusion from evidence.

unknowns.description: Project-specific facts or user intent that could not be established from the packet. Mark `critical` only when the skill would be wrong without the answer. Do not include questions answerable from general engineering expertise, or facts already in the packet.

question.description: A single, specific question, e.g. `Should refunds be processed synchronously or queued?`

importance.description: `critical`: blocks a correct skill. `optional`: a documented assumption is acceptable.

conflicts.description: Places where packet sources disagree (e.g. two Node versions).

subject.description: What the disagreement is about, e.g. `Node.js version`.

observations.description: The conflicting observations, one per source, e.g. [`.nvmrc pins 18`, `package.json engines requires >=20`].

sources.description: Packet evidence ids or repository-relative paths backing the observations.

additionalContextRequests.description: Optional targeted requests for project information missing from the packet. Keep them few and specific; never request a full scan.

contextRequest.description: A targeted, bounded request for more repository information (same contract as context-request.schema.json).

path.description: Repository-relative POSIX path; not absolute, no `..` segments.

query.description: What to look for when no exact path is known (dependency name, symbol).

reason.description: Why this information is needed for the task.

priority.description: `required` when the skill cannot be compiled correctly without it; otherwise `optional`.
